turns.doctor_question: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Well, I guess I’m here because everyone keeps acting like this whole foreclosure on my house is just... paperwork. You know, they keep saying it's just about missed payments. But I know for a fact that the bank, the loan servicer, and even people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. 

And speaking of my job, I supervise the sales floor at the retail center downtown, and let me tell you, managing those girls is a full-time headache on its own. Just last week, Sarah decided to reorganize the entire clearance section without asking me, and it took me three hours to fix the sizing run. Three hours! I had to stay until 10 PM. I don't even get overtime for that, which really isn't fair considering I went out of my way to get my associate's degree to get this promotion in the first place. The district manager doesn't even appreciate it. 

But... anyway, what was I saying? Right, the house. They're all in on it. And no amount of papers they try to show me is going to change what I’ve been seeing with my own two eyes for almost two years now. They think I don't notice, but I do.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed, persecutory belief that her bank, loan servicer, and coworkers are conspiring to push her out of her house, stating that no evidence or paperwork will change her mind.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangentiality, drifting from the topic of her foreclosure into a lengthy, unrelated story about her retail job and coworkers before losing her train of thought and having to redirect herself.

top_partial.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

turns.doctor_question: When you say you've been seeing things with your own two eyes for almost two years, have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people around you couldn't hear, or has it all been things you've observed visually?
turns.patient_response:
Voices? No, I mean... I'm not hearing things that aren't there. It's just what I see happening right in front of me. Like the cars, the looks people give each other... the paperwork. 

Which, honestly, speaking of paperwork, you should see the absolute disaster they leave in the back office at work. I swear, I spend half my shift just organizing the filing cabinet because corporate sends down these new promotional guidelines every single Tuesday, and the opening shift just shoves them in whatever folder they feel like. Last Tuesday, they put the new holiday return policy in the employee grievance file! I told the store manager, "You know this is how mistakes happen at the register, right?" But he just brushed me off. He brushes everything off. He's always on his phone during inventory anyway. I caught him texting the entire time we were doing the big denim reset last month. 

Denim is the absolute worst section to fold, by the way. If you don't use the plastic folding board, the stacks lean and it looks so trashy on the tables. The district manager hates leaning stacks, and guess who gets blamed for it? Me. Even though I wasn't even the one who folded them! 

But... wait, what did you ask me? Voices? No, no voices. Just regular things I see with my own eyes. I just actually pay attention to what's going on around me.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangential speech, drifting from the topic of hallucinations into a lengthy, unrelated complaint about workplace organization and folding denim, eventually forgetting the doctor's question.
symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly denies experiencing auditory hallucinations, stating they do not hear voices or things that are not there.

turns.doctor_question: If someone you trust completely—like a family member or close friend—showed you proof that the bank, your job, and these other people were NOT working together against you, would that change your mind, or do you believe you would still know the truth about what's really happening?
turns.patient_response:
Proof? Like what, more papers? Like I was just saying, everyone keeps acting like this whole foreclosure is just paperwork and missed payments. My sister actually tried that last month. She came over with a whole folder, acting like she had it all figured out to prove to me I was wrong. But like I told you, I know the bank, the loan servicer, and those people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. I don't care who shows me what. No amount of papers they show me changes what I’ve been seeing for almost two years. 

And honestly, speaking of my sister, she prints absolutely everything out. It drives me insane. She wastes so much ink. It’s exactly like the girls at the store. We have this new digital scheduling app now, right? Corporate spent thousands on it so we could go paperless. But Jessica—she's one of my main cashiers—she refuses to check her phone for her shifts. She literally makes me print out the weekly schedule and highlight her name in pink. Pink! If I use yellow highlighter, she claims she can't read it. And then she still shows up late! She was twenty minutes late on Saturday during the BOGO sale. Do you know how chaotic a BOGO sale gets in the accessories department? Customers just throw scarves everywhere. I spent an hour picking up pashminas off the floor while Jessica was in the breakroom complaining that the barista messed up her iced coffee. 

So... yeah, what were you asking? Right, proof. No, papers don't mean anything to me. I know what's actually happening.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient explicitly states that no amount of proof, even from a trusted sister, will change their fixed belief that people are conspiring to push them out of their house.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient's speech demonstrates tangentiality, wandering off-topic from the concept of proof to their sister's printing habits, a coworker's scheduling, and a store sale before finally returning to the original question.

turns.doctor_question: When you think about this situation with the bank and your job working together against you, is there any small part of you that thinks you might be mistaken, or are you completely certain that this is definitely happening?
turns.patient_response:
Mistaken? No. No, I am completely certain. There is no small part of me that thinks I'm wrong about this. Like I've been saying, they want me to think it's just missed payments and regular foreclosure paperwork, but I know they are all working together to push me out. The bank, the servicer, the people at work—it's all connected. And I know what I've seen for two years. 

Speaking of being mistaken, though, you wouldn't believe the mistakes corporate makes with our inventory counts. They sent us a shipment last week that was supposed to be all winter coats, right? Because it's getting cold. We cleared out the whole back wall for them. Took down all the autumn transition pieces, boxed them up, labeled them—which I had to do myself because nobody else knows how to use the label maker without jamming it. It’s not hard, you just have to make sure the tape is fed through the little plastic guide before you hit print! But anyway, we open the boxes from corporate, and guess what's inside? Swimsuits. Neon swimsuits. In November! 

I called the regional director, and she tried to tell me I must have misread the shipping manifest. Me! Misread it! I have an associate's degree, I know how to read a barcode. It’s just like how they try to tell me I'm misreading this whole house situation. They think if they just keep telling me I'm wrong, I'll eventually believe them. 

But... yeah, no. I'm not mistaken. I am one hundred percent sure about what they're doing with my house.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses complete certainty in their belief that the bank and their job are conspiring against them, demonstrating a fixed belief characteristic of delusions.

turns.doctor_question: Besides the bank, the loan servicer, and people at your job, do you believe there are other people or groups who are also involved in this plan against you, or is it just these specific people working together?
turns.patient_response:
No, it's just them. The bank, the servicer, and the people at work. I haven't seen anyone else involved. They're the only ones I've been watching coordinate this whole thing. 

Which honestly, coordinating things is something my team at work could really learn how to do. I mean, just yesterday I was trying to coordinate the lunch breaks. We only had three people on the floor because two people called out sick. Well, "sick." I know for a fact Kevin wasn't sick because I saw him post a picture of his dog at the park on his story. A golden retriever. Cute dog, honestly, but still. You don't leave your team stranded on a Saturday just to play fetch. 

Anyway, I'm trying to figure out how to cover the registers and the fitting rooms, and I tell Sarah—she's new, just started three weeks ago—I tell her to go to lunch at 1:00. What does she do? She goes at 12:30. Right in the middle of the lunch rush! And she didn't even tell anyone she was leaving! I turned around from helping a customer find a size 8 in the flare jeans—which we never have in stock because corporate always sends us too many size 2s and not enough 8s—and Sarah is just gone. Poof. Her register is logged out and the line is five people deep. 

I had to jump on register two, which has a sticky scanner button, by the way. I've put in three maintenance requests for that scanner. Three! But the IT guy says it's "not a priority." Everything is a priority when there's a line of angry customers holding sweaters they're going to complain about the price of anyway. 

So... wait, what did you ask me? Other people? No, no. Just the bank, the servicer, and the people at my job. That's it.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient maintains a fixed belief that specific groups (the bank, loan servicer, and coworkers) are coordinating a plan against them.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangential speech, going on a long, unrelated tangent about coworkers, lunch breaks, and store inventory before needing to ask what the original question was.

turns.doctor_question: When you think about the bank, the loan servicer, and your coworkers all working together to push you out of your house—is this something that could theoretically happen in the real world, or does it seem impossible according to the laws of nature or how the world actually works?
turns.patient_response:
Impossible? No, why would it be impossible? People do shady things in the real world all the time. Like I said, everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure is just paperwork and missed payments, like it's some normal administrative thing. But it's not magic, it's just corrupt people. I know the bank, the loan servicer, and even the people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. I've been seeing it happen right in front of me for almost two years now. It's completely possible because they're just using the system against me. 

Speaking of people thinking they can just do whatever they want in the real world, you know who else acts like that? The mall security guards. They have this whole little clique, it's ridiculous. I went down to the food court on my break on Tuesday to get a pretzel—the place with the cinnamon sugar ones, you know? And Paul, the head of security, was just standing there eating free samples and talking to the girl from the cell phone kiosk. Meanwhile, teenagers are practically skateboarding through my denim section! I had to yell at these kids myself because Paul was too busy flirting. 

And then he has the nerve to come into my store later and ask if we offer a mall employee discount on sunglasses. Sunglasses! You work indoors, Paul! What do you need aviators for? I told him no, obviously. Corporate is very strict about the discount policy anyway. We can only give it to immediate family, and even then, I have to swipe my manager card, and the new system prompts for a manager override code that changes every thirty days. I swear, corporate changes the password policy more often than we change the window displays. 

So... wait, what did you ask me? Magic or something? No, there's no magic or anything impossible happening. It's just real people doing this to my house.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed, false belief that the bank, loan servicer, and coworkers are conspiring to push them out of their house, which they maintain is a real-world plot.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangentiality, drifting from the topic of the foreclosure plot into a lengthy, unrelated story about mall security guards and corporate discount policies before forgetting the original question.

turns.doctor_question: Before almost two years ago when you started noticing this coordination between the bank, the loan servicer, and your coworkers, were you functioning well at work and in your personal life without these concerns?
turns.patient_response:
Before two years ago? Yeah, of course I was. And honestly, even now, when the foreclosure stuff isn't involved, I'm completely fine. I still get up every day for work, I supervise my team, I handle the schedules and customer issues... 

Which, by the way, handling customer issues has gotten so much worse lately. Just yesterday, this woman tried to return a pair of boots without a receipt. She didn't even have the box! Just carried them in a plastic grocery bag. And she was screaming at me because our policy says store credit only without a receipt. It's printed right on the register mat! Right where you set your purse down! But nobody reads anymore. I ended up having to give her the store credit on one of those little plastic gift cards, and the magnetic strip wouldn't swipe, so I had to type in the sixteen-digit number manually while she tapped her acrylic nails on the glass counter. Click, click, click. So rude. I swear, people lose their minds when they shop. 

But anyway, yeah, I handle all of that just fine. I take care of myself, my apartment is clean, I do my job. The problems really only start when I get mail, or bank calls, or when there's workplace paperwork that seems tied to what I know is happening with the house. That's when I have to drop everything and figure out what they're trying to pull. But if it's not about the house? I function perfectly well.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient describes a fixed belief that mail, bank calls, and workplace paperwork are part of a coordinated effort regarding their house, indicating a persecutory delusion.
symptom_reasoning.S023: The patient explicitly states they take care of themselves, keep their apartment clean, and do their job, denying avolition or diminished motivation.
symptom_reasoning.S025: The patient describes actively engaging in their work duties, supervising their team, and handling daily tasks, denying a loss of motivation or interest in daily activities.
